Abu Huraira confirmed hearing the Prophet tell Hassan bin Thabit to reply on his behalf, praying that Allah help him with the Holy Spirit.
Two companions leaving the Prophet on a dark night were lit by two lamp-like lights, one going with each when they parted until he reached home.
While building the mosque the Prophet wipes dust from Ammar, who carries two bricks at a time, saying a rebellious group will kill him as he calls them to Allah.
At Yamama Thabit bin Qais, perfuming himself with hunut, takes his place and refuses to flee; on the day of the Clans az-Zubair volunteers to scout, called the Prophet's disciple.
Abu Amir has an arrow drawn from his knee and the Prophet asks forgiveness for him; Sa'd comes armed at night to guard the Prophet, who then sleeps.
At the Trench Az-Zubair volunteers three times to scout the enemy, and the Prophet says every prophet has a disciple and his is Az-Zubair.
The Prophet always received Jarir with a smile, and when Jarir said he could not sit firm on horses, struck his chest and prayed he be firm and rightly guided.
Abu Dhar of Ghifar tells how Ali secretly led him to the Prophet in Mecca, where he embraced Islam and was twice beaten for declaring it, Al-Abbas shielding him.
Thabit bin Qais, fearing his voice raised over the Prophet's had annulled his deeds, was told that he is of the people of Paradise, not of the Fire.
Holy wars are won with a companion present, later a companion's companion, then theirs; the best are the Prophet's generation and the next, then come false witnesses.
The Prophet forbids abusing his companions, gives Abu Bakr, Umar and Uthman glad tidings of Paradise, and dreams of Abu Bakr and Umar drawing water; Ali prays for Umar.
Abu Huraira, often hungry beside the Prophet, calls Ja'far bin Abi Talib the most generous to the poor; Ibn Umar greets Ja'far's son as son of the two-winged one.
Uthman calls Az-Zubair the best and dearest to the Prophet, who names him his disciple and praises his scouting of Bani Quraiza; Az-Zubair is wounded charging at Al-Yarmuk.
Only Talha and Sa'd stayed by the Prophet in a battle; Talha's hand was paralysed shielding him, and Sa'd calls himself an early convert and first Arab archer for Allah.
The Prophet defends Usama's and Zaid's command; Usama alone dares intercede for a Makhzumi woman thief, and the Prophet says he would cut even Fatima's hand for theft.
Ibn Umar says the Prophet would have loved Usama's son and Al-Hajjaj, of Um Aiman's family, after making Al-Hajjaj repeat a faulty prayer; the Prophet asked Allah to love Usama.
Ibn Umar dreams angels take him to the Fire; the Prophet says Abdullah would be excellent if he prayed at night, and calls him a pious man.
Abu Ad-Darda praises Kufa's companions Ibn Mas'ud, Ammar and Hudhaifa and confirms Ibn Mas'ud's reading of 'By the Night'; the Prophet calls Abu Ubaida this nation's most trustworthy man.
Umar calls Bilal their chief, freed by Abu Bakr; the Prophet prays that Ibn Abbas be taught wisdom, and announces three flag-bearers martyred before Khalid takes the flag to victory.
The Prophet names Ibn Mas'ud first of four to learn the Quran from; Abu Ad-Darda confirms his reading, and Hudhaifa finds him most like the Prophet in conduct.
Ibn Abbas defends Mu'awiya's single-rak'a witr, as he was a companion and a learned man, and Mu'awiya says the Prophet forbade two rak'as after Asr.
Sa'd bin Mu'adh's handkerchiefs in Paradise surpass silk and the Throne shook at his death; he judges that Bani Quraiza's warriors be killed and their women and children taken captive.
Two men leaving the Prophet on a very dark night find a light before them, which divides to go with each when they part.
The Prophet names four to learn the Quran from, ranks the Ansar houses and recites to Ubai at Allah's order; Anas says four Ansar collected the Quran.
The Prophet calls Abdullah bin Salam a man of Paradise and reads his dream of a pillar as dying a Muslim; Abdullah warns that a debtor's gift is Riba.
The Prophet always smiles at Jarir bin Abdullah, who at his request destroys the pre-Islamic house of Dhul-Khalasa with 150 Ahmas horsemen, killing those found there, and is blessed.
Hind bint Utba, who once wished the Prophet's family degraded, now wishes it honoured; he lets her feed her children from miserly Abu Sufyan's property only what is reasonable.
Abu Dhar sends his brother to Mecca, then comes himself, is led to the Prophet by Ali, embraces Islam, and is beaten for proclaiming it until Al-Abbas rescues him.
Salman al-Farisi says he was sold from master to master more than ten times, comes from Ram-Hurmuz, and puts six hundred years between Jesus and Muhammad.
Abu Musa's party, whose boat took them to Ethiopia, reach the Prophet at Khaibar; he credits them with two migrations to Umar's one and knows the Ash'aris by their recitation.
At al-Ji'rana a bedouin rejects the Prophet's good tidings, so Abu Musa and Bilal accept them and drink and pour on themselves water he had washed in.
Amr bin al-As, commander at Dhat-us-Salasil, asks whom the Prophet loves most and hears Aisha, then her father, then Umar, then many other men.
The rulers of Najran, deciding against mutual cursing, ask for a trustworthy man, and the Prophet sends Abu Ubaida bin al-Jarrah, the most trustworthy of this nation.
Abu Musa, arriving from Yemen, at first takes Ibn Mas'ud and his mother for members of the Prophet's family, so often did they enter upon him.
Coming to Umar in a delegation, Adi bin Hatim is told he embraced Islam when his people disbelieved, kept promises they broke and recognised the truth they denied.
Allah orders the Prophet to recite Surah 98 to Ubai bin Ka'b, and Ubai weeps on learning that Allah mentioned him by name.
The Prophet names four companions to learn the Quran from; Ibn Mas'ud knows where every surah came down, four Ansar collected it, and Ubai was the best reciter.
Taunted as son of the woman of two waist-belts, Ibn az-Zubair heard from Asma that she split her belt to tie the Prophet's water skin and food container.
Hudhaifa said Ibn Um Abd most resembled the Prophet in bearing, piety and calm from leaving his house till returning, though none knew him alone with his family.
Ali never heard the Prophet say 'Let my father and mother be sacrificed for you' to anyone but Sa'd, as he shot arrows, perhaps at Uhud.
In a Medina garden the Prophet had Abu Musa open the gate with glad tidings of Paradise for Abu Bakr, Umar and Uthman, the last along with a coming calamity.
The best people are the Prophet's generation and those after them; later will come people who testify unasked, betray, break vows and grow fat.
When people criticised Usama's command, the Prophet swore his father Zaid had deserved command and was among those most beloved to him, as Usama was after him.
When people marvelled at a gift of soft silk, the Prophet swore that Sa'd's handkerchiefs in Paradise are better.
While Abu Musa kept the gate of a Medina garden, the Prophet gave Abu Bakr, Umar and Uthman glad tidings of Paradise, Uthman with a calamity to befall him.
The Prophet sent Abu Ubaida to the people of Najran as a truly trustworthy man, calling him the trustworthy one (Amin) of this nation.
Az-Zubair answered the Prophet's call three times at the Trench and was named his helper (hawari), and Abu Bakr, Umar and Uthman were given glad tidings of Paradise.
Wiping his nose on linen, Abu Huraira recalled fainting from hunger between the Prophet's pulpit and Aisha's dwelling, where passers-by thought him mad.
